stem: Insulin is transported around the body in the blood. The cells of the liver, muscle tissue and adipose (fat) tissue have receptors for insulin.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
State:
• the precise cellular location of the insulin receptors
• the type of biological molecule that forms an insulin receptor.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Insulin stimulates the activity of the enzyme glycogen synthetase in liver cells.
Fig. 7.1 shows the activity of glycogen synthetase in liver cells for $210\text{s}$ after glucose has been injected into the bloodstream.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Calculate the percentage increase in glycogen synthetase activity between $90\text{s}$ and $180\text{s}$ after glucose was injected into the blood.
Show your working and write your answer to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the role of glycogen synthetase in the regulation of blood glucose concentration.
